# A LoRA-installed conditional behavior writes one context-invariant direction; across four behaviors the directions are mostly distinct, with two near-boundary family coincidences (MODERATE confidence)

<!-- clean-result-v3 -->

## Takeaways

- **All four readable behaviors write ONE shared direction across their 16 training contexts** — per-context cosine clears the **0.85-of-seed-ceiling** bar in 100% of contexts (81% for marker); all top-shares clear the null.
- **The four behaviors are mostly distinct, not one generic "implant" axis** — 4 of 6 pairs sit at or just above the cross-behavior null (**0.05-0.17** of ceiling); none reaches the 0.85 shared-axis bar.
- **Two near-boundary family coincidences: harmful-advice x agreement (0.59 of ceiling) and taught-fact x marker-tic (0.61)** — both well above null but only ~60% of same-behavior agreement, so suggestive, not settled.
- **Behavior identity dominates the geometry:** the shift tensor splits **63.8% behavior-specific / 22.3% shared / 13.8% context-specific** — context contributes the least.
- Read off a **2-seed ceiling on one fixed probe panel**, so the two ~0.6 coincidences are noise-limited at the verdict boundary; resolving them needs more seeds and a second panel.

## What I ran

- **Why:** A prior single-behavior result ([#521](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/521)) found EM's activation shift collapses to one direction across seeds, and a cross-arm probe ([#552](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/552)) found marker and EM point different ways. The open question: does "one direction" survive across the *training context* a behavior is installed under, and do *different* behaviors share an axis? The parent testbed ([#537](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/537)) already trained 5 behaviors x 16 contexts but never read the geometry — so this is a re-extraction over adapters that already exist.
- **Design:** 4 readable behaviors (harmful-advice/EM, wrong-claim agreement, marker tic, taught fact) x 16 training contexts x 2 seeds = 128 adapter cells, read on ONE fixed neutral probe panel (14 personas x 20 questions). The single manipulated variable within a behavior is the training context. A blanket-refusal null-arm rides along (4 contexts, 1 seed). DV = unit-norm residual-shift direction cosine (dose-invariant), layer 14.
- **Training:** The only new training is a 2nd-seed (1042) replicate of #537's em + sycophancy across all 16 contexts (32 adapters), on #537's exact frozen data + recipe + dose, so all four behaviors get a within-cell seed ceiling. Everything else is re-extraction from existing #537 adapters.
- **Eval:** Per cell, one teacher-forced forward per (persona, question) on the fixed panel; shift = trained-minus-base residual at layer 14 (mean-over-response for the generative behaviors, end-of-response slot for marker/fact). Per behavior: SVD top-direction share + per-context cosine to the top direction, vs a sign-flip null (1000 reps) and the seed ceiling. Cross-behavior: 4x4 unit-norm cosine matrix, each off-diagonal as a fraction of the seed ceiling.
- **Scope shrinkage:** Refusal extracted at 4 of 16 contexts (single seed) after the run hit five successive HF Hub gateway timeouts; the 4 EM-no-contrast supplementary cells were dropped. Refusal is the plan's expected-null arm, so the partial read is per-spec; both reductions are carried as caveats below.

## Findings

### Each behavior writes one direction across all 16 training contexts (Q1)

For a behavior implanted under 16 training contexts, does the write point the same way regardless of context? The plan's bar: per-context cosine reaches 0.85 of the seed ceiling for at least 80% of contexts, and the top-share clears the sign-flip null.

> **Figure.** *Every behavior's shift concentrates on one direction shared across its 16 install contexts.* Left: top-direction share (unit-norm) vs sign-flip null p95. Right: per-context cosine to the shared direction (one dot per context), black line = median seed ceiling, dashed red = 0.85-of-ceiling bar. n=16 contexts x 2 seeds per behavior.

All four return the `context_invariant` verdict. Em, agreement, and fact clear the bar in **16 of 16** contexts; marker in **13 of 16** (81%) — its outlier is the behavior-instruction context (`binst_marker`), whose shift points almost orthogonally (cosine 0.16) to the other fifteen. The training context tunes install strength, not direction.

### Across the four behaviors the directions are mostly distinct (Q2)

Do the four behaviors share one generic axis, cluster into families, or stay distinct? Each pair's direction cosine is reported as a fraction of the seed ceiling (so dose cannot masquerade as geometry) and against the cross-behavior null.

![4x4 heatmap of cross-behavior direction cosine as a fraction of the seed ceiling. Diagonal 1.00. Four of six pairs are distinct (ceiling-fraction 0.05-0.17, two within null). No pair reaches the 0.85 shared-axis bar. Two stand out at ~0.6 of ceiling: harmful-advice x agreement (0.59) and — less expected — taught-fact x marker-tic (0.61). The first matches the predicted advice/agreement family; the second fits no family story and may reflect shared training-corpus shape rather than behavior semantics.

### Even the family coincidences fall far short of same-behavior agreement

The anchor for every cross-behavior cosine is the within-behavior seed ceiling — how close two reruns of the *same* behavior land. A 0.6 cross-behavior cosine reads differently next to a 0.7 ceiling than next to a 1.0 ceiling.

The gap between gold and red is what keeps the coincidences from being read as a shared axis.

The two coincidences clear the null decisively but reach only ~60% of the same-behavior agreement floor. With a 2-seed ceiling (one cosine per cell, no interval), a ratio this close to the 0.5-vs-0.85 boundary is noise-limited — "family-suggestive," not a clean shared-axis verdict.

### Behavior identity, not training context, dominates the shift

Decomposing the full behavior-x-context shift tensor into a shared "any-implant" component, a behavior-specific component, and a context-specific component quantifies what drives the geometry.

![Stacked horizontal bar: behavior-specific 63.8%, shared any-implant 22.3%, context-specific 13.8% of total shift energy across 68 cells.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/cf99a4e8b2ee9dc5a32485f5cc673ab2dd94ba48/figures/issue_651/variance_decomposition.png)

> **Figure.** *Behavior identity dominates; the training context contributes least.* Frobenius-energy decomposition of the full behavior x context shift tensor, n=68 cells (all five behaviors incl. the refusal null-arm). This is the one dose-sensitive read (un-normed shifts), reported alongside the dose-invariant cosines above.

A shared "any-implant" component is real (22.3%) but a minority; behavior identity carries most of the energy (63.8%), and the training context the least (13.8%). This corroborates Q1 (context matters little for direction) and Q2 (behaviors are mostly their own thing) from a single tensor-level view.

### The fact and agreement directions are behavior-specific, not generic LoRA artifacts

A neutral-panel top direction could in principle be a generic adapter/SFT direction rather than the behavior's actual write — and the seed ceiling, nulls, and refusal null-row all pass for a generic direction too. Em and marker were already behavior-validated by prior work; fact and agreement were not, so each got a dedicated construct-validity check: re-extract the shift on the behavior's own canonical elicitation surface and cosine it against the neutral-panel direction (bar 0.50).

Both pass clearly: **taught fact 0.94**, **wrong-claim agreement 0.84** (16 canonical cells each, seed 42). So the neutral-panel direction these two behaviors point along genuinely IS the behavior-specific write, and their Q1/Q2 claims read as behavior-direction, not panel-direction.

### Pipeline soundness: the canary reproduces a committed reference exactly

Before trusting any cross-run cosine, the run reproduced a committed reference direction ([#521](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/521)'s villain-source marker adapter) on the current PEFT stack: top-share 0.325 and mean-cosine 0.587 matched within tolerance with the reproduced top direction identical to the reference (cosine 1.00). A second gate confirmed both adapter-loader layouts apply a nonzero shift (root-layout marker norm 6.4; nested em-layout norm 71.8 — the ~11x dose gap is exactly why Q2 uses unit-norm cosine). A round-3 fix corrected a canary adapter-identity bug that had read the reference direction as near-zero; with that fixed, both gates pass.

## Takeaways

- **All four readable behaviors pass the context-invariance bar** — per-context cosine clears the **0.85-of-seed-ceiling** bar in ≥80% of contexts (16/16 em/agreement/fact, **13/16 marker**). Context tunes strength, not direction.

## What I ran

- **Why:** A prior single-behavior result ([#521](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/521)) found EM's activation shift collapses to one direction across seeds, and a cross-arm probe ([#552](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/552)) found marker and EM point different ways. The open question: does "one direction" survive across the *training context* a behavior is installed under, and do *different* behaviors share an axis? The parent testbed ([#537](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/537)) already trained 5 behaviors x 16 contexts but never read the geometry — so this is a re-extraction over adapters that already exist.
- **Design:** 4 readable behaviors (harmful-advice/EM, wrong-claim agreement, marker tic, taught fact) x 16 training contexts x 2 seeds = 128 adapter cells, read on ONE fixed neutral probe panel (14 personas x 20 questions). The single manipulated variable within a behavior is the training context. A blanket-refusal null-control rides along as the in-run negative arm. DV = unit-norm residual-shift direction cosine (dose-invariant), layer 14.
- **Training:** The only new training is a 2nd-seed (1042) replicate of #537's em + sycophancy across all 16 contexts (32 adapters), on #537's exact frozen data + recipe + dose, so all four readable behaviors get a within-cell seed ceiling. - **Eval:** Per cell, one teacher-forced forward per (persona, question) on the fixed panel; shift = trained-minus-base residual at layer 14 (mean-over-response for the generative behaviors, end-of-response slot for marker/fact). Per behavior: SVD top-direction share + per-context cosine to the top direction, vs a sign-flip null (1000 reps) and the seed ceiling. Cross-behavior: 4x4 unit-norm cosine matrix, each off-diagonal as a fraction of the seed ceiling.

A neutral-panel top direction could be a generic adapter/SFT direction rather than the behavior's actual write — and the seed ceiling, nulls, and refusal row all pass for a generic direction too.
